notes.title: March 29 Patch Notes
notes.content:
Dear Players,

Thank you for your support of Miryam: The Polluted Land! Today, we’ve released a new patch update, adjusting the difficulty of certain levels and optimizing the overall gameplay experience based on player feedback.

[h3]Update Details[/h3]
🔹 Adjustments
1. Reduced the difficulty of the first 9 levels to make it easier for new players to get started.

🔹 New Features
2. Added an option to skip cutscenes, so you can jump straight into the action.

🔹 Optimizations
3. Improved targeting behavior for defensive structures to enhance combat accuracy.
4. Made the skip button for the prologue cutscene more visible and easier to use.

We’ll continue to listen to your feedback and improve the game! If you encounter any issues while playing, feel free to share them in the community—we’ll work on fixes as soon as possible.

Thank you for your support, and enjoy the game!

— Miryam: The Polluted Land Development Team

notes.title: Miryam: The Polluted Land – Now Available on Steam!
notes.content:
Embark on an unforgettable journey through the Land of Nod in this innovative tower defense game developed by 6.5F Studio and published by Vsoo Games. With a rich narrative, strategic gameplay, and unique enemies, Miryam: The Polluted Land offers a fresh and immersive twist on the classic tower defense genre.

[h1]Game Features[/h1]
[list]
[*] 40+ Unique Enemies: Face a variety of grotesque creatures, each with its own attack patterns and weaknesses.
[*] 20+ Defensive Structures: From explosive clay pots to moths that clear fog, strategically deploy defenses to fend off the horrors.
[*] 40+ Challenging Levels: Test your strategic skills in diverse stages with increasing difficulty.
[*] A Dark Storyline: Follow Miryam’s journey through the haunted Land of Nod as she battles creatures born from her own fears.
[/list]

In Miryam: The Polluted Land, you won’t just be defending your territory—you’ll be facing your past. The game’s narrative dives deep into Miryam’s journey of overcoming her inner demons while defending against nightmarish enemies.

Available Now on Steam – Get 10% Off for the First Two Weeks!
Don’t miss out on the launch discount—Miryam: The Polluted Land is available for $4.99/£4.29/€4.99 (or your local equivalent). Act fast to grab this limited-time offer!

notes.title: Playtest Recruitment
notes.content:
Dear Guardians!

We are conducting a pre-launch playtest to identify technical issues and ensure the game is in its optimal state. This is a closed, limited-scale test. Interested Guardians should:

[*] Join our Discord community

Applications will be randomly approved. If selected, you'll receive a notification email from Steam. Please do NOT share gameplay footage/videos on social media before the official launch.

Note:
The test version includes 30 levels (vs. 40+ in the full release)

Team Miryam

notes.title: Between the Walls and the Wounds
notes.content:
Miryam was on the brink. At school, those nasty kids relentlessly mocked her clothes and accent, sometimes even pelting her with stones. At home, her mother’s world revolved around the newborn, leaving Miryam with nothing but orders—"Make the formula!" "Get the diapers!" "Be quiet!" Resentment coiled inside her, tightening day by day, until one evening, she whispered to her little brother a wish she didn’t fully mean:

"I wish you would disappear."

And then, he was gone. As if the universe had heard her plea—and obeyed. But the price was steep. Miryam herself was cast into the Land of Nod, a cursed, forsaken place where reality twisted, and shadows whispered her name.

In this unfamiliar world, she met the Cultivator, a figure draped in mystery. He offered her a bargain: help him cleanse the land of its monstrous corruption, and in return, he would help her find her brother and a way home. It wasn’t much of a choice—what else could she do?

But the creatures she faced were beyond anything she could comprehend.

When the wooden javelin-wielding Kaomen lurked in the distance, she saw—what? The echoes of familiar voices? Just like the three girls at school who laughed at her in the hallway, whispering cruel things behind their hands. When the Blue Lizardmen slashed at her with their filthy claws, she could almost hear the sharp, cutting words spoken to her at home. The "Lust" dispersed a mist that reminded her of the lies she had to swallow daily, the way truths were twisted and obscured by those who were supposed to protect her.

And then there were the mosquitoes. Their tiny, buzzing faces—they looked just like that annoying boy from her class. The one who mocked her every day, always finding new ways to make her feel small. She crushed them with a single strike, their bodies popping like overripe berries. It felt... good.

For all its horrors, something about this world felt honest. More honest than school, where cruelty wore friendly masks. More honest than home, where love was conditional. The monsters didn’t pretend; they attacked, and she fought back. And every time she struck them down, she felt an intoxicating sense of control.

The Cultivator’s promises began to sound hollow. Did he truly know how to send her home? Did she even want to go back?

As the bonfires burned and the fences held back the tide of creatures, Miryam faced a question greater than any monster before her:

Was she searching for her brother, or running from herself?
